info.title: Personal Agent API
info.description: Conversations with a Personal Agent and the Companies it works with over PAP 1.0: messages, quick replies, proposals and their approval, sign-in and events; and the agent account, with its passkeys and the session of each device. A browser's requests are the playground's own, by its cookies, from its origin. A client app sends no Origin: it creates an account or signs in with a passkey, then sends `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.

get.summary: An app's sign-in link (`SignIn.url`), opened in the app's browser: it starts the sign-in there and goes on to the Company's consent page. It works once, within three minutes, for the account, conversation, Company and access it was made for. Used, expired, of a session that ended, or opened in a browser signed in to another account, it goes to `endUrl` with `?result=failed`.

303.description: To the Company's consent page, or to `endUrl` with `?result=failed`.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events: `state` first, then what changes (a sign-in finished, a proposal expired or replaced, a Company's message in a Direct Conversation). Closes after five minutes or when the conversation ends; open it again. A signed-in stream ends with `session.ended` within seconds of its session ending or its access token running out. An account keeps at most ten streams open (`too_many_streams`).

CompanyRef.description: A Company, named by its origin; `name` is to show.

Answer.description: What a choice carries, in place of a message. Exactly one member; Companies are named by origin and nothing here is read as words.

Choice.description: A quick reply. Show `label`; send `answer` to `answers`, never the label as a message.

AgentMessage.description: Something said. `agent` without `company` is the agent's own voice about the conversation; `company` is a Company's own words, to show as theirs.

Proposal.description: A change a Company holds for the User's approval, with its exact terms. Nothing is performed until it is approved.

ModelChoice.description: The model a turn is asked of, with the User's own key; demo mode, which runs scripted examples only, when left out. `free` is the deployment's own small model, with no key: each turn needs a Turnstile token (`turnstile`) for the deployment's site key, and one without a good token, or past the free model's limits, runs in demo mode with a line that says why.

SignIn.description: What to open for the sign-in. The agent never sees a password. For the playground's page, `url` is the Company's own consent page. For a client app, `url` is a page of the agent's own, a link that works once, before `expiresAt` (milliseconds since 1970): open it at once in a browser of the app's own, such as ASWebAuthenticationSession. It goes on to the Company's consent page, and the browser comes back to `endUrl` with `?result=done` or `?result=failed`, which is what the app watches for. The conversation's events say how it went.

AgentEvent.description: An event of the stream; its `type` is also the SSE event name. `state` comes first.

code.description: For `session.ended`: `invalid_token` when the access token ran out or was replaced (refresh it and open the stream again), `session_revoked` when the device was signed out.

Error.description: `error` is written for the User and can be shown as it is.

Passkey.description: One of the account's passkeys. `name` is the device it was added on, in that device's words; `synced` says a password manager keeps it on the person's other devices too. Its key is never shown.

Account.description: An agent account: an opaque ID, its passkeys and the label the person chose, and nothing else about them. `session` is the session of this request; `unclaimed`, for a browser only, counts its own conversations from before it signed in.

SessionTokens.description: A client app's tokens. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer`; it lasts about 15 minutes. Exchange the refresh token at `/api/v1/sessions/refresh` for new ones: each works once, and one used twice ends the session. Keep both in the device's keychain, never in a URL or a log. Times are milliseconds since 1970.

SignedIn.description: The account, signed in on this device. A browser is given a cookie and no `tokens`; a client app, which sends no `Origin`, is given `tokens`.

CreationOptions.description: WebAuthn options for `navigator.credentials.create` (PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON), and the ceremony to answer them with within five minutes, once.

RequestOptions.description: WebAuthn options for `navigator.credentials.get` (PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON) with no username: any of this site's passkeys answers. Answer within five minutes, once.

PasskeyAnswer.description: The authenticator's answer (RegistrationResponseJSON or AuthenticationResponseJSON) to the ceremony's options. `device` names this device in its own words, such as "iPhone" or "Chrome on macOS".

Session.description: A device signed in to the account. `current` is the one this request is made with.

LinkCode.description: A one-time code to type into a channel, which links it to the account. It works once, for five minutes.

apiSession.description: An API session's access token (`SessionTokens`). A browser on the playground's own origin uses its cookie instead.
